questions.qtext:
We say a set of attributes $X$ is closed (with respect to a given set of FD's) if $\mathrm{X}^{+}=\mathrm{X}$.

For which of the following set of functions dependencies does the relation $R(A, B, C, D)$ has $AB, CD$ as closed sets?

options.text: $A \rightarrow B, B \rightarrow C, C \rightarrow D, D \rightarrow A$
$A \rightarrow B, B \rightarrow A, C \rightarrow A, D \rightarrow A$
$A \rightarrow B, B \rightarrow A, C \rightarrow D, D \rightarrow C$

questions.solution:
Answer: A, D

Selected solution (score: 10)

"Closed" Set of Attributes, Definition:

We say a set of attributes $X$ is closed (with respect to a given set of FD’s) if $X^+ = X.$ (Source: Ullman Book for DBMS)

So, $AB$ is closed iff $(AB)^+ = AB.$

$CD$ is closed iff $(CD)^+ = CD$

So, answer will be Option A & D.

Watch this Beautiful question on this concept: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EU5O_8wH3Xw&t=1157s

questions.qtext:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets of attributes.
Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: If a relation has no attribute that is functionally determined by all the other attributes combined, then the relation has no nontrivial FD's at all.
If $\mathrm{X} \subseteq \mathrm{Y}$, then $\mathrm{X}^+\subseteq \mathrm{Y}^+$ (where the closures are taken with respect to the same set of FD's)
If $A B \rightarrow C$ and $A \rightarrow C$, then $B \rightarrow C$.

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C

Source solution 1 (score: 6)

Detailed Video Solution:

Option A: Detailed Video Solution - Ullman Book Question

Option B: Detailed Video Solution - Ullman Book Question

Option C: Detailed Video Solution - Ullman Book Question

Option D: Detailed Video Solution - Ullman Book Question

Source solution 2 (score: 1)

Answer is $\boxed{A,B,C}$

A. If a relation has no attribute that is functionally determined by all the other attributes combined, then the relation has no nontrivial FD's at all.

Lets assume we have a Relation with R(A,B,C) with only 1 non-trivial functional dependencies {$A\to B$} , we can extrapolate the FD as $AC\to B$. We can easliy conclude that since the contrapositive if given statemen true , the statement itself becomes true.

B. If X⊆Y, then X+⊆Y+ (where the closures are taken with respect to the same set of FD's)

This is straightaway true.

C. $(X^+)^{+} = X^+$

This is true because closure of a set of attributes is equal to closure of clsoure of set of attributes. This property is known as Idempotency of Attribute Closure

D. If AB→C and A→C, then B→C.

This need not be true, if we have $AB\to C$ and $A\to C$ then it need not be the case that $B\to C$ is true. Hence this is false.

questions.qtext:
Consider a relation $\mathrm{R}\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C})$ such that each attribute functionally determines the other two attributes. Relation R and its FD's have several minimal bases.
Which of the following is/are a minimal base (canonical cover) for FDs of R ?
questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C

Selected solution (score: 3)

Detailed Video Solution: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EU5O_8wH3Xw&t=4140s

Answer is option $\boxed{A,B,C}$

Original FD :{ ${ A \to B, A \to C,
B \to A, B \to C,
C \to A, C \to B }$ }

A) $A \to B, B \to A, B \to C, C \to B$

$\boxed{\text{check for minimal}}$

remove $A \to B$ and using remaining functional dep. find out if we can determine $B$ from $A$.

$A^+ : A \ \times$ NOPE, hence $A \to B$ is not redundant functional dependency.

lets check if $B \to A$ is Redundant.

$B^+ : BC \ \times$ we can't determine $A$ from $B$. hence $B \to A$ is not Redundant.

lets check if $B \to C$ is redundant

$B^+ : BA \ \times$ Not redundant.

lets check if $C \to B$ is redundant.

$C^+ : C \ \times$ NOT Redundant.

Hence This FD set is minimal.

$\boxed{\text{check for cover}}$

$A^+ : ABC$
$B^+ : BCA$
$C^+ : CBA$

which covers the original set of functional dependency.

Hence option A is correct coz its minimal cover of FDs of R.

B) $A \to B, B \to C, C \to A$

$\boxed{\text{check for minimal}}$

yes its minimal.

$\boxed{\text{check for cover}}$

$A^+ : ABC$
$B^+ : BCA$
$C^+ : CAB$

It covers FDs of R.

Hence option B is correct.

C) $A \to C, B \to C, C \to A, C \to B$

$\boxed{\text{check for minimal}}$

$A^+ : A$ , hence $A \to C$ is not Redundant.

$B^+ : B$ , hence $B \to C$ is not Redundant aswell

$C^+ : CB$ , hence $C \to A$ is not redundant aswell

$C^+ : CA$ , hence $C \to B$ is also not Redundant.

Hence this set of FDs are minimal.

$\boxed{\text{check for cover}}$

$A^+ : ACB$ yes, it covers FDs of R.

$B^+ : BCA$

$C^+ : CBA$

Hence option C is correct.

D) $A \to C, B \to C, C \to A$

$\boxed{\text{check for minimal}}$

yes its minimal

$\boxed{\text{check for Cover}}$

$A^+ : AC$ $\rightarrow$ Doesn't determine $B$

$B^+ : BCA$

$C^+ : CA$ $\rightarrow$ Doesn't determine $B$

Hence not a cover of FDs of R.

option D is wrong.
